security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown fences and inline documentation. One high-risk finding is confirmed because SKILL.md presents eval(expression) in a function tool, which can execute arbitrary Python if copied. No prompt injection language was found, but the FastAPI example also exposes raw exception messages.

remediation.issue: Unsafe calculator tool uses eval on model-supplied expressions.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval with a constrained expression parser or explicit arithmetic operations, and remove the unsafe example from the main path.

remediation.issue: FastAPI example returns raw exception text to clients.
remediation.suggestion: Log server errors internally and return a generic response body from public endpoints.

remediation.issue: External weather tool lacks timeout and privacy notes.
remediation.suggestion: Add httpx timeouts, input validation for city, and a note that user data is sent to wttr.in.

remediation.issue: Quick start shows an API key placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: State that users must store keys in local environment variables or secret managers and never commit them.

content.user_title: Build OpenAI Agents With SDK Patterns
content.value_statement: Agent projects need clear structure before tool calls, handoffs, and guardrails become hard to manage. This skill provides reusable OpenAI Agents SDK patterns for Python teams.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to define Agents with instructions, models, and structured outputs.
Demonstrates async, sync, streamed, and continued Runner execution patterns.
Provides examples for function tools, typed tool inputs, and context-aware tools.
Explains multi-agent routing with handoffs and agents used as tools.
Includes guardrail examples for input validation and output validation.
Outlines a FastAPI integration and a suggested project structure.
limitations: Examples are instructional and require dependency setup before use.
It targets the OpenAI Agents SDK, not LangChain or raw OpenAI API workflows.
Security hardening is partial; unsafe examples must be replaced before production.
It does not provide a complete generated project or deployment pipeline.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Python Agent Service
use_cases.description: Use the templates to create async agents, tool functions, and a FastAPI endpoint for early product validation.

use_cases.title: Design Multi-Agent Routing
use_cases.description: Combine specialist agents with handoffs so user requests reach the right agent for each task.

use_cases.title: Create Tutoring Agents
use_cases.description: Adapt the tutor, guardrail, and context examples for guided lessons and practice workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to scaffold a simple OpenAI Agents SDK assistant. Include agent instructions, the Runner call, and setup notes.

prompt_templates.title: Add Function Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to add typed function tools to an existing agent. Include safe input validation and explain each tool boundary.

prompt_templates.title: Build Multi-Agent Handoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a triage agent with three specialists. Include routing logic, handoff descriptions, and conversation continuation.

prompt_templates.title: Harden a Production Agent API
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to review an agent service design for guardrails, streaming, context handling, observability, and production security gaps.

output_examples.input: Create a beginner tutoring agent for Python concepts.
output_examples.output: A plan with a tutor agent, async runner flow, structured instructions, and guardrail recommendations.

output_examples.input: Add a weather lookup tool to an assistant.
output_examples.output: A tool design summary with typed inputs, validation notes, timeout guidance, and agent wiring steps.

output_examples.input: Design a triage flow for support questions.
output_examples.output: A multi-agent routing outline with specialist roles, handoff descriptions, and conversation continuation guidance.

best_practices: Replace demonstration eval calls with a constrained parser or vetted calculation library.
Set explicit timeouts and validation for every external tool or network request.
Use guardrails to define tool boundaries, allowed topics, and output requirements.
anti_patterns: Copying sample code into production without replacing unsafe placeholders.
Letting model-selected tool inputs reach external services without validation.
Returning raw exception messages from public API endpoints.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a full project?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that you adapt into your project.

faq.question: Which SDK does it target?
faq.answer: It targets the OpenAI Agents SDK for Python.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill content is compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it cover streaming responses?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a streamed Runner example and a FastAPI streaming pattern.

faq.question: Is the included calculator tool production safe?
faq.answer: No. Replace the eval example with safe parsing before any production use.

faq.question: Does it cover multi-agent workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes handoffs and agents-as-tools patterns for specialist routing.
